subject: maths
title: Converting Units
seo_title: Year 5 Converting Units Worksheets: Metric, Imperial and Time (Free, with Answers)
standard_text: Convert between different units of metric measure [for example, kilometre and metre; centimetre and metre; centimetre and millimetre; gram and kilogram; litre and millilitre]; understand and use approximate equivalences between metric units and common imperial units such as inches, pounds and pints; solve problems involving converting between units of time; use all four operations to solve problems involving measure [for example, length, mass, volume, money] using decimal notation, including scaling.
meta_desc: Free Year 5 maths worksheets on converting units: km, m, cm and mm, kg and g, l and ml with decimals, imperial units (inches, feet, pounds and pints), and time including leap years. Scales and word problems with recipes and money. 100 questions with an answer key, matched to the National Curriculum.
key_big: Bigger unit to smaller unit: multiply. Smaller unit to bigger unit: divide.
key_sub: 2.4 km = 2,400 m and 350 g = 0.35 kg. Time uses 60, so 1 hour = 60 minutes, not 100. Imperial units are only about: 1 inch ≈ 2.5 cm, 1 kg ≈ 2.2 lb, 1 pint ≈ 570 ml.
body_html:
Multiply or divide?

To change a bigger unit into a smaller unit, multiply: you need more of the small units. To change a smaller unit into a bigger unit, divide. Multiplying by 1,000 moves every digit 3 places to the left. Dividing by 1,000 moves every digit 3 places to the right.

Kilometres to metres

2.4 km = ☐ m

1 km = 1,000 m. Multiply: 2.4 × 1,000 = 2,400.

Answer: 2,400 m (not 240 m)

Grams to kilograms

350 g = ☐ kg

1 kg = 1,000 g. Divide: 350 ÷ 1,000 = 0.35.

Answer: 0.35 kg

Metric facts to know

MeasureFacts
Length1 cm = 10 mm   1 m = 100 cm   1 km = 1,000 m
Mass1 kg = 1,000 g
Capacity1 l = 1,000 ml

Read the scale, then convert

Work out what each mark is worth before you read the scale.

Imperial units

Imperial units are older units that are still used in the UK. Milk is sold in pints, people often give their height in feet and inches, and babies are weighed in pounds (lb). We only need rough facts, so we say about (≈).

ImperialAbout the same as
1 inch2.5 cm
1 foot (12 inches)30 cm
2.2 pounds (lb)1 kg
1 pint570 ml (just over half a litre)
Inches to centimetres

12 inches ≈ ☐ cm

1 inch ≈ 2.5 cm. 12 × 2.5 = 30.

Answer: about 30 cm

Pints to litres

4 pints ≈ ☐ litres

1 pint ≈ 570 ml. 4 × 570 = 2,280 ml = 2.28 l.

Answer: about 2.3 litres

Time is not decimal

An hour has 60 minutes, not 100, and a minute has 60 seconds.

TimeFacts
Seconds and minutes1 minute = 60 seconds   1 hour = 60 minutes
Days and weeks1 day = 24 hours   1 week = 7 days
Years1 year = 12 months = 52 weeks and 1 day = 365 days
Leap yearsevery 4 years, 366 days, with 29 February (2024, 2028)
Hours to minutes

2 hours 15 minutes = ☐ minutes

2 × 60 = 120. 120 + 15 = 135.

Answer: 135 minutes

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
2.4 km = 240 m1 km = 1,000 m, so multiply by 1,000: 2.4 km = 2,400 m
1 km = 100 mKilo means 1,000: 1 km = 1,000 m and 1 kg = 1,000 g
Multiplying to get a bigger unit (350 g = 350,000 kg)Smaller unit to bigger unit: divide (350 g = 0.35 kg)
1 hour = 100 minutes1 hour = 60 minutes, so 130 minutes = 2 hours 10 minutes
4 pints = exactly 2,280 mlImperial facts are approximate: 4 pints is about 2.3 litres

faq.q: What unit conversions do Year 5 children need to know?
faq.a: Year 5 children convert between km and m, m and cm, cm and mm, kg and g, and l and ml, often with decimals. They also convert units of time and learn rough imperial equivalents such as inches, pounds and pints.

faq.q: Do Year 5 pupils learn imperial units?
faq.a: Yes. They learn approximate equivalences, such as 1 inch ≈ 2.5 cm, 1 foot ≈ 30 cm, 1 kg ≈ 2.2 lb and 1 pint ≈ 570 ml, because these units are still used in everyday life in the UK.

faq.q: How do you convert kilometres to metres?
faq.a: Multiply by 1,000, because 1 km = 1,000 m. So 2.4 km = 2,400 m. To go back from metres to kilometres, divide by 1,000.

faq.q: How many days are in a leap year?
faq.a: A leap year has 366 days instead of 365, because February has 29 days. Leap years come every 4 years, such as 2024 and 2028.

sets.title: Length: mm, cm, m and km with decimals

items.q: Convert. 3 km = ☐ m
items.e: 1 km = 1,000 m. Kilometres are bigger than metres, so multiply by 1,000: 3 × 1,000 = 3,000. The digits move 3 places to the left. So 3 km = 3,000 m. (300 m would mean 1 km = 100 m.)

items.q: Convert. 5,000 m = ☐ km
items.e: 1 km = 1,000 m. Metres are smaller than kilometres, so divide by 1,000: 5,000 ÷ 1,000 = 5. The digits move 3 places to the right. So 5,000 m = 5 km.

items.q: Convert. 4 m = ☐ cm
items.e: 1 m = 100 cm. Metres are bigger than centimetres, so multiply by 100: 4 × 100 = 400. The digits move 2 places to the left. So 4 m = 400 cm.

items.q: Convert. 600 cm = ☐ m
items.e: 1 m = 100 cm. Centimetres are smaller than metres, so divide by 100: 600 ÷ 100 = 6. The digits move 2 places to the right. So 600 cm = 6 m.

items.q: Convert. 8 cm = ☐ mm
items.e: 1 cm = 10 mm. Centimetres are bigger than millimetres, so multiply by 10: 8 × 10 = 80. The digits move 1 place to the left. So 8 cm = 80 mm.

items.q: Convert. 2.4 km = ☐ m
items.e: 1 km = 1,000 m. Kilometres are bigger than metres, so multiply by 1,000: 2.4 × 1,000 = 2,400. The digits move 3 places to the left. So 2.4 km = 2,400 m. (240 m multiplies by 100, not 1,000.)

items.q: Convert. 350 m = ☐ km
items.e: 1 km = 1,000 m. Metres are smaller than kilometres, so divide by 1,000: 350 ÷ 1,000 = 0.35. The digits move 3 places to the right. So 350 m = 0.35 km.

items.q: Convert. 1.5 m = ☐ cm
items.e: 1 m = 100 cm. Metres are bigger than centimetres, so multiply by 100: 1.5 × 100 = 150. The digits move 2 places to the left. So 1.5 m = 150 cm.

items.q: Convert. 3.7 cm = ☐ mm
items.e: 1 cm = 10 mm. Centimetres are bigger than millimetres, so multiply by 10: 3.7 × 10 = 37. The digits move 1 place to the left. So 3.7 cm = 37 mm.

items.q: Convert. 85 mm = ☐ cm
items.e: 1 cm = 10 mm. Millimetres are smaller than centimetres, so divide by 10: 85 ÷ 10 = 8.5. The digits move 1 place to the right. So 85 mm = 8.5 cm.

items.q: Convert. 0.75 km = ☐ m
items.e: 1 km = 1,000 m. Kilometres are bigger than metres, so multiply by 1,000: 0.75 × 1,000 = 750. The digits move 3 places to the left. So 0.75 km = 750 m.

items.q: Convert. 125 cm = ☐ m
items.e: 1 m = 100 cm. Centimetres are smaller than metres, so divide by 100: 125 ÷ 100 = 1.25. The digits move 2 places to the right. So 125 cm = 1.25 m.

items.q: Convert. 2,050 m = ☐ km
items.e: 1 km = 1,000 m. Metres are smaller than kilometres, so divide by 1,000: 2,050 ÷ 1,000 = 2.05. The digits move 3 places to the right. So 2,050 m = 2.05 km. The 0 in 2,050 keeps its place: 2.05, not 2.5.

items.q: Convert. 4.06 m = ☐ cm
items.e: 1 m = 100 cm. Metres are bigger than centimetres, so multiply by 100: 4.06 × 100 = 406. The digits move 2 places to the left. So 4.06 m = 406 cm. (460 cm would be 4.6 m.)
The pencil starts at 2 cm, not 0. It ends 4 small marks after 9 cm, at 9.4 cm. 9.4 − 2 = 7.4 cm (74 mm). 9.4 cm forgets that the pencil does not start at 0.

items.q: Convert. 3 km 400 m = ☐ km
Which is the same as 1.08 m?
Which is the longest?
items.e: Change them all to metres: 0.65 km = 650 m, 0.6 km = 600 m and 6,500 cm = 65 m. 650 m is the longest. 6,500 has the biggest number, but centimetres are small.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: 250 ÷ 100 = 2.5, so 250 cm = 2.5 m. The others are wrong: 3.5 km = 3,500 m, 60 mm = 6 cm and 0.4 m = 40 cm.

items.q: Find the missing number. 1 m − 35 cm = ☐ m
items.e: 1 m = 100 cm. 100 − 35 = 65 cm. 65 ÷ 100 = 0.65 m. Take care when you exchange: 100 − 35 is 65, not 75.

sets.title: Mass and capacity: g, kg, ml and l

items.q: Convert. 4 kg = ☐ g
items.e: 1 kg = 1,000 g. Kilograms are bigger than grams, so multiply by 1,000: 4 × 1,000 = 4,000. The digits move 3 places to the left. So 4 kg = 4,000 g.

items.q: Convert. 6,000 ml = ☐ l
items.e: 1 l = 1,000 ml. Millilitres are smaller than litres, so divide by 1,000: 6,000 ÷ 1,000 = 6. The digits move 3 places to the right. So 6,000 ml = 6 l.

items.q: Convert. 2.5 kg = ☐ g
items.e: 1 kg = 1,000 g. Kilograms are bigger than grams, so multiply by 1,000: 2.5 × 1,000 = 2,500. The digits move 3 places to the left. So 2.5 kg = 2,500 g.

items.q: Convert. 1.5 l = ☐ ml
items.e: 1 l = 1,000 ml. Litres are bigger than millilitres, so multiply by 1,000: 1.5 × 1,000 = 1,500. The digits move 3 places to the left. So 1.5 l = 1,500 ml.

items.q: Convert. 350 g = ☐ kg
items.e: 1 kg = 1,000 g. Grams are smaller than kilograms, so divide by 1,000: 350 ÷ 1,000 = 0.35. The digits move 3 places to the right. So 350 g = 0.35 kg. Check: 0.35 kg is a bit more than a quarter of a kilogram.

items.q: Convert. 750 ml = ☐ l
items.e: 1 l = 1,000 ml. Millilitres are smaller than litres, so divide by 1,000: 750 ÷ 1,000 = 0.75. The digits move 3 places to the right. So 750 ml = 0.75 l.

items.q: Convert. 0.25 kg = ☐ g
items.e: 1 kg = 1,000 g. Kilograms are bigger than grams, so multiply by 1,000: 0.25 × 1,000 = 250. The digits move 3 places to the left. So 0.25 kg = 250 g.

items.q: Convert. 3.2 l = ☐ ml
items.e: 1 l = 1,000 ml. Litres are bigger than millilitres, so multiply by 1,000: 3.2 × 1,000 = 3,200. The digits move 3 places to the left. So 3.2 l = 3,200 ml.

items.q: Convert. 80 g = ☐ kg
items.e: 1 kg = 1,000 g. Grams are smaller than kilograms, so divide by 1,000: 80 ÷ 1,000 = 0.08. The digits move 3 places to the right. So 80 g = 0.08 kg. You need a 0 in the tenths place.

items.q: Convert. 1,250 ml = ☐ l
items.e: 1 l = 1,000 ml. Millilitres are smaller than litres, so divide by 1,000: 1,250 ÷ 1,000 = 1.25. The digits move 3 places to the right. So 1,250 ml = 1.25 l.

items.q: Convert. 2 kg 50 g = ☐ kg
Work out 1.2 l + 600 ml. Give your answer in litres.
items.e: Use one unit first: 600 ml = 0.6 l. Then 1.2 + 0.6 = 1.8 l. 601.2 l adds the numbers without converting.

items.q: Which is the heaviest?
items.e: Change them all to grams: 1 kg 600 g = 1,600 g, 1.5 kg = 1,500 g and 0.95 kg = 950 g. 1,600 g is the heaviest.

items.q: Which list goes from the smallest to the largest capacity?
items.e: Change them all to millilitres: 0.3 l = 300 ml and 0.5 l = 500 ml. 300 < 450 < 500.

items.q: The scale shows the mass of some carrots. What is the mass in kilograms?
items.e: The numbers go up by 200 g and there are 4 spaces, so each mark is 50 g. The needle is 3 marks past 600 g: 600 + 150 = 750 g. 750 ÷ 1,000 = 0.75 kg. (0.63 kg counts each mark as 10 g.)

items.q: The scale shows the mass of a bag of potatoes. What is the mass in kilograms?
items.e: Each kilogram is split into 5 equal spaces, so each mark is 1 ÷ 5 = 0.2 kg (200 g). The needle is 3 marks past 2 kg: 2 + 0.6 = 2.6 kg. (2.3 kg counts each mark as 0.1 kg.)

items.q: The scale shows the mass of a parcel. What is the mass in kilograms?
items.e: Each kilogram is split into 4 equal spaces, so each mark is 1 ÷ 4 = 0.25 kg (250 g). The needle is 3 marks past 1 kg: 1 + 0.75 = 1.75 kg. (1.3 kg counts each mark as 0.1 kg.)

items.q: How much water is in the jug? Give your answer in litres.
items.e: The numbers go up by 250 ml and there are 5 spaces, so each line is 50 ml. The water is 2 lines above 750 ml: 750 + 100 = 850 ml. 850 ÷ 1,000 = 0.85 l. (0.77 l counts each line as 10 ml.)

items.q: How much water is in the jug? Give your answer in litres.
items.e: The numbers go up by 500 ml and there are 5 spaces, so each line is 100 ml. The water is 3 lines above 1,000 ml: 1,300 ml. 1,300 ÷ 1,000 = 1.3 l. (1.15 l counts each line as 50 ml.)

items.q: How much more water is needed to fill the jug to 2 litres?
items.e: Each line is 100 ml. The water is at 1,200 ml. 2 litres = 2,000 ml. 2,000 − 1,200 = 800 ml more. (1,200 ml is the water already in the jug.)

sets.title: Imperial units: inches, feet, pounds and pints

items.q: About how many centimetres are the same as 1 inch?
items.e: This is the fact to learn: 1 inch ≈ 2.5 cm. An inch is about the width of an adult’s thumb. (12 is the number of inches in 1 foot.)

items.q: About how many centimetres are the same as 1 foot?
items.e: This is the fact to learn: 1 foot ≈ 30 cm, about the length of a school ruler. 1 foot = 12 inches, and 12 × 2.5 = 30. (100 cm is 1 metre.)

items.q: About how many pounds (lb) are the same as 1 kg?
items.e: This is the fact to learn: 1 kg ≈ 2.2 lb. A pound is a bit less than half a kilogram, so there are more pounds than kilograms. (1 kg = 1,000 g, not 1,000 lb.)

items.q: About how many millilitres are the same as 1 pint?
items.e: This is the fact to learn: 1 pint ≈ 570 ml, which is just over half a litre. (1,000 ml is 1 litre, not 1 pint.)

items.q: A bottle holds 1 pint of milk. Which is closest to its capacity?
c: about a quarter of a litre
items.e: 1 pint is about 570 ml. Half a litre is 500 ml, so 570 ml is just over half a litre.
Follow the red line from 4 inches down to the centimetres: it is just past 10 cm. Or work it out: 1 inch is about 2.5 cm. 4 × 2.5 = 10, so 4 inches ≈ 10 cm. (6.5 cm adds 4 + 2.5.)

items.q: About how many centimetres are the same as 12 inches?
items.e: 1 inch is about 2.5 cm. Inches are bigger than centimetres, so multiply: 12 × 2.5 = 30 cm. 12 inches is 1 foot, which is about 30 cm. (4.8 cm divides instead.)

items.q: About how many inches are the same as 20 cm?
items.e: 1 inch is about 2.5 cm. Centimetres are smaller, so divide: 20 ÷ 2.5 = 8 inches. Check: 8 × 2.5 = 20. (50 inches multiplies instead.)

items.q: About how many centimetres are the same as 3 feet?
items.e: 1 foot is about 30 cm. 3 × 30 = 90 cm. (36 is the number of inches in 3 feet, not centimetres.)

items.q: About how many pounds (lb) are the same as 5 kg?
items.e: 1 kg is about 2.2 pounds (lb). 5 × 2.2 = 11 lb. There are more pounds than kilograms. (7.2 lb adds 5 + 2.2.)

items.q: A suitcase can weigh up to 20 kg. About how many pounds (lb) is that?
items.e: 1 kg is about 2.2 pounds (lb). 20 × 2.2 = 44 lb (2 × 22). (440 lb puts the decimal point in the wrong place.)

items.q: About how many kilograms are the same as 22 lb?
items.e: 1 kg is about 2.2 pounds (lb). Pounds to kilograms: divide. 22 ÷ 2.2 = 10 kg. Check: 10 × 2.2 = 22. (48.4 kg multiplies by 2.2 instead.)

items.q: About how many millilitres are the same as 2 pints?
items.e: 1 pint is about 570 ml. 2 × 570 = 1,140 ml. (285 ml halves 570 instead of doubling it.)

items.q: About how many litres are the same as 4 pints?
items.e: 1 pint is about 570 ml. 4 × 570 = 2,280 ml. 2,280 ml = 2.28 l, which is about 2.3 litres. (4 l treats a pint as a litre.)

items.q: Which is the longest?
items.e: Change them all to centimetres. 1 foot ≈ 30 cm, 11 inches ≈ 11 × 2.5 = 27.5 cm, and 0.2 m = 20 cm. 1 foot is the longest.

items.q: Which is heavier: a 2 kg bag of flour or a 4 lb bag of flour?
c: You cannot compare kg and lb
items.e: 1 kg is about 2.2 pounds (lb). 2 kg ≈ 2 × 2.2 = 4.4 lb, which is more than 4 lb. So the 2 kg bag is heavier. 4 is the bigger number, but a pound is lighter than a kilogram.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: 1 foot is about 30 cm. The others are wrong: 1 inch ≈ 2.5 cm, 1 kg ≈ 2.2 lb and 1 pint ≈ 570 ml, just over half a litre.

items.q: Ava is 4 feet 6 inches tall. About how tall is she in centimetres?
items.e: 4 feet ≈ 4 × 30 = 120 cm. 6 inches ≈ 6 × 2.5 = 15 cm. 120 + 15 = 135 cm. (126 cm adds 6 cm instead of 6 inches.)

items.q: Freya’s baby brother weighed 6.6 lb when he was born. About how much is that in kilograms?
items.e: 1 kg is about 2.2 pounds (lb). Pounds to kilograms: divide. 6.6 ÷ 2.2 = 3 kg. Check: 3 × 2.2 = 6.6. (14.52 kg multiplies instead. A newborn baby is not that heavy.)

items.q: A recipe needs 1 pint of milk. George has a 1 litre carton. Is there enough?
c: Yes, with exactly 430 ml left over
Yes, with about 430 ml left over
Yes, with about 530 ml left over
No, he needs about 430 ml more
items.e: 1 pint is about 570 ml. 1 litre = 1,000 ml, which is more than 570 ml. 1,000 − 570 = 430 ml left over. It is about 430 ml, not exactly, because 1 pint ≈ 570 ml is an approximation.

sets.title: Time: seconds to years and leap years

items.q: Convert. 4 hours = ☐ minutes
items.e: 1 hour = 60 minutes (not 100). Multiply: 4 × 60 = 240, so 4 hours = 240 minutes.

items.q: Convert. 5 minutes = ☐ seconds
items.e: 1 minute = 60 seconds. Multiply: 5 × 60 = 300, so 5 minutes = 300 seconds.

items.q: Convert. 180 seconds = ☐ minutes
items.e: 1 minute = 60 seconds. Seconds to minutes: divide by 60, not 100. 180 ÷ 60 = 3, because 3 × 60 = 180.

items.q: Convert. 300 minutes = ☐ hours
items.e: 1 hour = 60 minutes. Minutes to hours: divide by 60. 300 ÷ 60 = 5. (3 hours divides by 100, as if 1 hour were 100 minutes.)

items.q: Convert. 3 days = ☐ hours
items.e: 1 day = 24 hours. Multiply: 3 × 24 = 72, so 3 days = 72 hours. (36 hours uses 12 hours, which is only half a day.)

items.q: Convert. 6 weeks = ☐ days
items.e: 1 week = 7 days. Multiply: 6 × 7 = 42, so 6 weeks = 42 days.

items.q: Convert. 56 days = ☐ weeks
items.e: 1 week = 7 days. Days to weeks: divide. 56 ÷ 7 = 8, so 56 days = 8 weeks.

items.q: Convert. 4 years = ☐ months
items.e: 1 year = 12 months. Multiply: 4 × 12 = 48, so 4 years = 48 months. (52 is the number of weeks in a year.)

items.q: Convert. 2 hours = ☐ seconds
items.e: 1 hour = 60 minutes and 1 minute = 60 seconds, so 1 hour = 60 × 60 = 3,600 seconds. 2 × 3,600 = 7,200 seconds. (120 is the number of minutes.)

items.q: How many days are in a leap year?
items.e: A normal year has 365 days. A leap year has one extra day, 29 February, so it has 366 days.

items.q: Which of these years is a leap year?
items.e: A leap year comes every 4 years. Leap years divide exactly by 4: 2028 ÷ 4 = 507. 2025, 2026 and 2030 do not divide exactly by 4, so they are not leap years.

items.q: How many days are in February in a leap year?
items.e: February usually has 28 days. In a leap year it has one extra day, 29 February, so it has 29 days.

items.q: How many days are in 2 years? Neither year is a leap year.
items.e: 1 year = 365 days. 2 × 365 = 730 days. (104 is the number of weeks in 2 years, and 732 days would be 2 leap years.)

items.q: Convert. 2 hours 15 minutes = ☐ minutes
items.e: 2 hours = 2 × 60 = 120 minutes. Add the 15 minutes: 120 + 15 = 135 minutes. (215 minutes would mean 1 hour = 100 minutes.)

items.q: Which is the same as 200 seconds?
items.e: 3 minutes = 180 seconds. 200 − 180 = 20, so 200 seconds = 3 minutes 20 seconds. (2 minutes would mean 1 minute = 100 seconds.)

items.q: Which is the same as 1.5 hours?
items.e: 0.5 hours is half an hour, and half of 60 minutes is 30 minutes. So 1.5 hours = 1 hour 30 minutes = 90 minutes, not 1 hour 50 minutes.

items.q: Which is the same as 130 minutes?
items.e: 120 minutes = 2 hours. 130 − 120 = 10, so 130 minutes = 2 hours 10 minutes. 1 hour 30 minutes and 1.3 hours both treat an hour as 100 minutes.

items.q: Which is the longest time?
items.e: Change them all to minutes: 1.5 hours = 90 minutes, 1 hour 45 minutes = 105 minutes and 6,000 seconds = 6,000 ÷ 60 = 100 minutes. 110 minutes is the longest.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: 1 day = 24 hours, and each hour is 60 minutes. 24 × 60 = 1,440, so 1 day = 1,440 minutes. 2,400 minutes uses 100 minutes in an hour.

items.q: Find the missing number. 3 minutes − 45 seconds = ☐ seconds
items.e: 3 minutes = 3 × 60 = 180 seconds. 180 − 45 = 135 seconds. (255 seconds uses 300 seconds for 3 minutes. 225 adds instead of subtracting.)

sets.title: Word problems: recipes, money and journeys

items.q: A recipe for 4 people uses 200 g of flour. How much flour is needed for 6 people?
items.e: 200 ÷ 4 = 50 g for each person. 6 × 50 = 300 g. (202 g adds 2 instead of scaling, and 1,200 g is 6 × 200.)

items.q: A pancake recipe for 4 people uses 300 ml of milk. How many litres of milk are needed for 10 people?
items.e: 300 ÷ 4 = 75 ml for each person. 10 × 75 = 750 ml. 750 ÷ 1,000 = 0.75 l. (3 l uses 300 ml for each person.)

items.q: Isla’s family drinks 2 pints of milk every day. About how many litres is that in 1 week?
items.e: 1 week = 7 days, so 7 × 2 = 14 pints. 1 pint ≈ 570 ml, so 14 × 570 = 7,980 ml, which is about 8 litres. (14 l treats a pint as a litre. 1.1 l is only 1 day.)

items.q: A 1.5 litre bottle of water is shared equally between 6 cups. How much water goes in each cup?
items.e: 1.5 l = 1,500 ml. 1,500 ÷ 6 = 250 ml. Check: 6 × 250 = 1,500. (0.25 is the answer in litres, not ml.)

items.q: Apples cost £1.20 for 1 kg. How much do 2.5 kg of apples cost?
items.e: 2 kg cost 2 × £1.20 = £2.40. Half a kilogram costs half of £1.20, which is 60p. £2.40 + 60p = £3. (£2.40 forgets the 0.5 kg. £3.70 adds 2.5 instead of multiplying.)

items.q: Cheese costs 90p for 100 g. How much does 0.5 kg of cheese cost?
items.e: 0.5 kg = 500 g. 500 g is 5 lots of 100 g. 5 × 90p = 450p = £4.50. (45p works out 0.5 × 90p without converting. £9 is the price of 1 kg.)

items.q: Arjun has 3 m of ribbon. He cuts it into pieces 25 cm long. How many pieces does he get?
items.e: 3 m = 300 cm. 300 ÷ 25 = 12 pieces. (4 pieces is only 1 m. 75 pieces multiplies 3 × 25.)

items.q: One lap of the school track is 400 m. Lily runs 6 laps. How far does she run in kilometres?
Noah walks 850 m to school. He walks there and back every day for 5 school days. How far does he walk in the week, in kilometres?
items.e: There and back is 2 × 850 = 1,700 m a day. 5 × 1,700 = 8,500 m. 8,500 ÷ 1,000 = 8.5 km. (4.25 km forgets the walk home. 1.7 km is only 1 day.)

items.q: Poppy posts three parcels. They weigh 1.4 kg, 650 g and 2 kg. What is their total mass in kilograms?
items.e: Change 650 g to kilograms first: 650 ÷ 1,000 = 0.65 kg. 1.4 + 0.65 + 2 = 4.05 kg. (9.9 kg treats 650 g as 6.5 kg.)

items.q: A film lasts 135 minutes. It starts at 6:30 pm. What time does it finish?
items.e: 135 minutes = 120 + 15 = 2 hours 15 minutes. 6:30 pm + 2 hours = 8:30 pm, then 15 more minutes is 8:45 pm. (8:05 pm reads 135 minutes as 1 hour 35 minutes.)

items.q: Freya practises the piano for 20 minutes every day for 2 weeks. How long is that altogether?
items.e: 2 weeks = 14 days. 14 × 20 = 280 minutes. 4 × 60 = 240, and 280 − 240 = 40, so it is 4 hours 40 minutes. (2 hours 80 minutes uses 100 minutes in an hour. 2 hours 20 minutes is only 1 week.)

items.q: Oliver’s summer holiday is 3 weeks and 4 days long. How many days is that?
items.e: 1 week = 7 days, so 3 weeks = 21 days. 21 + 4 = 25 days. (19 days counts only 5 days in a week.)

items.q: A real car is 10 times as long as a model of it. The model is 42 cm long. How long is the real car in metres?
items.e: The real car is 10 times as long: 42 × 10 = 420 cm. 420 ÷ 100 = 4.2 m. (420 m forgets to change centimetres to metres.)

items.q: A cake recipe for 8 people uses 1.2 kg of flour. How many grams of flour are needed for 2 people?
items.e: 2 people is a quarter of 8 people. 1.2 kg = 1,200 g. 1,200 ÷ 4 = 300 g. (600 g is enough for 4 people. 4,800 g multiplies by 4 instead of dividing.)

items.q: Grace’s dad is 6 feet tall. About how tall is he in metres?
items.e: 1 foot ≈ 30 cm, so 6 feet ≈ 6 × 30 = 180 cm. 180 ÷ 100 = 1.8 m. (0.72 m changes 6 feet into 72 inches, then reads them as centimetres.)

items.q: Leo buys 4 pints of milk. Each pint costs 65p. How much does he pay?
A 5 kg bag of rice is shared equally into 8 smaller bags. How many grams of rice are in each bag?
items.e: 5 kg = 5,000 g. 5,000 ÷ 8 = 625 g. Check: 8 × 625 = 5,000. (0.625 is the answer in kilograms, not grams.)

items.q: Four pupils do a standing long jump. Oliver jumps 1.45 m, Ava jumps 138 cm, Leo jumps 1,520 mm and Isla jumps 1.5 m. Who jumps the furthest?
items.e: Change them all to centimetres: 1.45 m = 145 cm, 1,520 mm = 152 cm and 1.5 m = 150 cm. 152 cm is the furthest, so Leo jumps the furthest.

items.q: Mohammed’s family goes on holiday on 25 July. The holiday lasts exactly 3 weeks. On what date do they come home?
items.e: 3 weeks = 21 days. July has 31 days, so 25 July + 6 days = 31 July. 21 − 6 = 15 days more: 15 August. (16 August counts July as 30 days. 28 July adds 3 days, not 3 weeks.)
